newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA MANUEL SAYS FX MOVES A SIGN OF CONFIDENCE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA MANUEL SAYS FX MOVES A SIGN OF CONFIDENCE.

text.p: The relaxation of foreign exchange controls on South African individuals bore testimony to the government's growing sense of confidence, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Tuesday.
From Tuesday, South Africans were allowed to invest up to 200,000 rand in offshore assets for the first time since 1961 when exchange controls were introduced.
"The significance of this change cannot be underestimated," Manuel said in a speech prepared for delivery at the South African Chamber of Business' annual banquet.

"In line with our new democracy and in fulfilling our mandate and commitment to create a competitive, growing and job absorbing economy, the steps taken today bear testimony to our growing sense of confidence," he said.

Manuel said latest reserves data, released at 1600 GMT, also reflected increasing confidence in the South African economy -- a factor which had been apparent in government's recent roadshows to the U.S. and Japan where it successfully launched a Yankee and Samurai bond.
The Reserve Bank said earlier that South Africa's gold and foreign exchange reserves grew 300 million rand to 22.1 billion rand in June.
The central bank has been building up its reserves and access to credit lines in anticipation of the relaxation of foreign exchange controls on Tuesday.

Governor Chris Stals said last week the bank had access to 38 billion rand in reserves and credit lines which it could use to smooth any market volatility resulting from demand for foreign currency by local individuals.
On the day, the markets firmed as the rand held its ground to trade at 4.5285/5315 against the dollar from 4.5280/5310 on Monday.
